svg.title: Lakehouse-to-Power-BI BI serving over OneLake with Direct Lake
svg.desc: An original architecture diagram for serving interactive Power BI reports from a Fabric lakehouse. Curated gold Delta tables in a lakehouse persist one physical copy on OneLake. A Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model binds to those tables by a framing operation and lazily loads only the columns a query touches into capacity memory. Power BI report visuals live-connect to that model and issue DAX queries. All of it — Spark writes, OneLake reads, the semantic model, and report queries — draws capacity units from a single Fabric F-SKU capacity, whose size sets the per-model memory bound. A warning band flags that exceeding that memory bound causes cold reads from OneLake, and that OneSecurity on the source lakehouse can force a DirectQuery fallback.
svg.text: Lakehouse → Power BI over OneLake with Direct Lake — Serving Architecture
Single open Delta Parquet copy on OneLake · Direct Lake lazy column load · Capacity F-SKU memory boundary
ZONE 1: ACTIVE READ / SERVE HIGHWAY (DAX ➔ LAZY LOAD)

g.aria-label: Power BI report visuals live-connected to the semantic model
g.title: Report visuals — live-connect to the published semantic model and issue DAX; no data is copied into the report.

g.aria-label: Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model
g.title: Direct Lake on OneLake semantic model — reads Delta columns straight from OneLake, no import, no SQL round trip; never falls back.

g.aria-label: Curated gold Delta tables in the Fabric lakehouse
g.title: Gold lakehouse tables — one physical Delta/Parquet copy; the same tables every Fabric engine reads.

g.aria-label: Column residency states in capacity memory
g.title: Column residency — a model sits in cold, semiwarm, warm, or hot state; latency improves at each step, bounded by SKU memory.
g.text: Evicts on: framing · idle · RAM pressure

g.aria-label: Warning: memory bound overshoot and OneSecurity fallback
g.title: Warnings — exceeding the SKU memory bound causes cold reads from OneLake at peak; OneSecurity on the source lakehouse can force DirectQuery fallback.
g.text: CRITICAL GUARDRAILS & FAILURE MODES TO DESIGN AROUND
• Memory Bound Overshoot: Exceeding capacity limit forces columns into cold reads from OneLake at peak (high latency, not error).
• OneSecurity Fallback Trap: OneLake data-access roles on source lakehouse can push the model into DirectQuery fallback.

g.aria-label: OneLake — the single physical Delta/Parquet copy every Fabric engine reads
g.title: OneLake — one physical Delta/Parquet copy of the lakehouse's gold tables; every Fabric engine, including the Direct Lake model, reads the same files with no second copy.
g.text: Single physical Delta/Parquet copy on OneLake. Direct Lake reads columns directly with no refresh pipelines.
Delta Lake Format · Tables Area · Multi-Engine Interop (Spark / SQL Endpoint / Power BI)

svg.text: SINGLE FABRIC F-SKU CAPACITY — COMPUTE POOL & MEMORY BOUNDARY

g.aria-label: Fabric capacity sizing for this BI-serving design
g.title: Capacity — the F-SKU sets the per-model Direct Lake memory bound and meters all CU consumption; F64+ unlocks free-license report viewing.
